trial_court: learned Addl. District Judge, Goalpara in Misc. (J) Case No. 05/2021
case_name: Ghana Shyam Das vs Mule Bala Das
facts_of_case: Petitioner's estranged wife sought pendente lite maintenance and expenses of proceeding under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The respondent claimed she was compelled to leave the petitioner's company with their minor son in 2015. A maintenance proceeding was instituted against the petitioner under Section 125 Cr.P.C., which was tried by the learned Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bongaigaon.

legal_principles.principle: The power of the Courts to grant maintenance under the provisions of section 125 Cr.P.C. as well as section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 can both stand together.
legal_principles.held: It has been held by the Supreme Court of India that such remedy has also been held to be a measure of social justice to prevent wives from falling into destitute and vagrancy.

legal_principles.principle: It is mandatory for the parties to file their respective affidavit regarding disclosure of assets and liabilities.
legal_principles.held: The Supreme Court of India had laid down the law that it was mandatory for the parties to file their respective affidavit regarding disclosure of assets and liabilities.

outcome.final_order: The impugned order dated 25.02.2022 is set aside and the matter is remanded to the trial court for fresh disposal.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: respondent's application for pendente lite maintenance
